fact.text: An Indiana homeowner was so proud of his house's design that he wore neckties with patterns inspired by its architect.

heads_up: Gruodį pensijų priemokos bus išmokėtos iš karto už du mėnesius.
Nuo gruodžio aplinkosaugininkai nebebudės po darbo – pažeidimai gali būti tiriami lėčiau.

lithuania.headline: Nuo sausio elektra brangs ketvirtadaliu, dujos – per 40 proc.
lithuania.summary: Premjeras Mindaugas Sinkevičius sako, kad nuo sausio elektra brangs ketvirtadaliu, o dujos – daugiau nei 40 proc.; Vyriausybė jau parengė energetikos įmonių viršpelnio mokesčio juodraštį, o koalicija ieško būdų sumažinti 3,8 proc. BVP siekiantį deficitą.
lithuania.context: Seimas rudenį grąžino 2027 m. biudžeto projektą Vyriausybei tobulinti, nes planuojamas deficitas viršija ES leidžiamus 3 proc. BVP. Koalicija jau sutarė didinti lošimų, cukraus mokesčius ir alkoholio bei tabako akcizus, o mokytojai streikuoja reikalaudami didesnių algų; biudžetas turėtų būti priimtas gruodį.

lithuania.headline: Nausėda: kalbos apie ataką prieš Kaliningradą – „burbulas“
lithuania.summary: Prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda „šimto procentų garantija“ teigia, kad iš Lietuvos jokie dronai į Kaliningrado sritį neskrido, o ministras Robertas Kaunas sako, kad radarai nieko neužfiksavo ir tai buvo psichologinė operacija, siekiant išprovokuoti Lietuvos reakciją.
lithuania.context: Lapkričio 21 d. vakarą Kaliningrado srityje suskambo oro pavojaus sirenos, o srities gubernatorius užsiminė apie objektą „iš Lietuvos pusės“. Rusijos kanalai per kelias valandas tai pavertė teiginiais, kad Rusiją puolė Ukraina ar NATO iš Lietuvos, nors Lietuvos oficialiai niekas nekaltino.

lithuania.headline: Kongo DR paleisti septyni Lietuvos piliečiai
lithuania.summary: Kongo DR rugsėjo 28 d. šnipinėjimu įtarti sulaikyti septyni 30–45 metų lietuviai paleisti po derybų, kuriose dalyvavo prezidento patarėjas Deividas Matulionis; pasak pareigūnų, jie buvo turistai ir neturėjo nei dronų, nei ginklų.
lithuania.context: Jie buvo sulaikyti Kinšasoje, nes fotografavo saugomą objektą ir kalbėjosi su kariu.

world.headline: NATO vows to defend against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
world.summary: NATO chief Mark Rutte vowed to defend the alliance in space after German media reported that Russia could launch 'Sputnik-S', a satellite carrying a nuclear warhead, as early as December; the Kremlin dismissed the reports.
world.why: Covered by 6 outlets, BBC front page
world.context: A nuclear blast in orbit could knock out thousands of satellites, including Starlink and the ISS, and would break the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which Russia signed.

world.headline: EU proposes 22nd Russia sanctions package, targeting banks, crypto and sport
world.summary: Ursula von der Leyen proposed cutting 60 more Russian banks from SWIFT, a crypto sanctions task force, a visa ban for Russians who fought in Ukraine and a ban on Russian teams and athletes competing under their flag in the EU.
world.context: The EU has imposed sanctions on Russia since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has now listed more than 4,200 people and entities. Each package needs the approval of all 27 member states.

world.headline: Burnham says rejoining the EU would need a referendum
world.summary: UK prime minister Andy Burnham told MPs it would be 'unthinkable' to rejoin the EU without another referendum, his strongest pledge yet, while saying there is 'no fixed destination' and attacking former Tory leaders as 'stuck in the past'.
world.why: Covered by 5 outlets, top of UK front pages
world.context: Britain voted to leave the EU in 2016 and left in 2020. Burnham, who says he personally would prefer to rejoin, reopened the debate this autumn and plans to set out options for closer ties next month.

world.headline: 14 countries back ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide
world.summary: Fourteen countries, including the UK, Canada, Australia and Spain, formally recognised last week's ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, and the UK sanctioned five senior Myanmar military leaders.
world.context: In 2017 Myanmar's army killed about 10,000 Rohingya and drove more than 700,000 into Bangladesh. Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and last week the court ruled 9–6 that it committed genocide, the first time a state has been found guilty of the crime.

interesting.headline: GTA 6 is the biggest launch in PlayStation history
interesting.summary: Sony says over 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5 in its first four days, logging 683 million hours, after the game made a record $3.79bn in day-one sales and scored 99 on Metacritic.

interesting.headline: Spielberg to direct a western with Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley
interesting.summary: Steven Spielberg will direct a western starring Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley, with Paul Thomas Anderson writing the script based on 'The Heart in Winter'.

interesting.headline: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents approve code
interesting.summary: Anthropic's Claude Ship adds two beta agents to its code reviewer: PR Steward fixes failing checks and merge conflicts, and Claude Approvals approves routine changes under a team-written policy.

interesting.headline: Ladybird, the first new browser engine in years, opens for testing
interesting.summary: After more than four years of work, the independent Ladybird browser, with an engine built from scratch rather than on Chrome, Safari or Firefox, launched in alpha on macOS and Linux.

ongoing.title: Nvidia CEO's affair with alleged Chinese spy
ongoing.update: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman 11 days after he resigned, after Trump said he convinced the board; shares jumped about 30%, adding almost $1tn, while the US blacklisted Megaspeed and Huang is due to testify to the Senate next week.
ongoing.context: Huang, Nvidia's co-founder, resigned in November after admitting an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, who was later reported to be in contact with Chinese intelligence. The company was accused of funnelling Nvidia AI chips to China, and the board at first refused his offer to return.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Ukraine confirmed seven naval drones sank the new Russian corvette Merkury and hit a cargo ship in Libya's Benghazi, a Russian strike on a Zaporizhzhia apartment block killed two, and the Pentagon is delaying Patriot missiles for Ukraine.
ongoing.context: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. Ukraine pushed Russian forces back from Kyiv and later in the east and south, and the war has since become a grinding fight of drones, missiles and attacks on energy, increasingly spilling beyond Ukraine's borders.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran said three ships caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and its top negotiator ruled out talks until the US meets seven conditions, while Qatar's prime minister tries to revive them.
ongoing.context: Tensions rose after the US withdrew from the 2015 nuclear deal in 2018 and reimposed sanctions. They escalated into open strikes between Israel, the US and Iran, and fighting has since spread to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for the world's oil.
